bib.title: Agent Primitives: Reusable Latent Building Blocks for Multi-Agent Systems

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Agent Primitives: Reusable Latent Building Blocks for Multi-Agent Systems", Haibo Jin, Peng Kuang, Ye Yu, Xiaopeng Yuan, Haohan Wang (UIUC). Proceedings of the 43rd ICML, PMLR 306, 2026. arXiv:2602.03695v2, 24 May 2026.

COVERAGE: 19 of 19 pages, 83,497 of 83,497 chars. This includes the appendices (prompts, extra results, ablations, efficiency tables) and the references, which I skimmed. Extraction was clean. The figure captions script was not run. Figure 1 is described from the text only.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- claim: The paper decomposes multi-agent systems (MAS) into three reusable "primitives": Review (Solver plus Critic loop), Voting and Selection (parallel Solvers plus a Selector), and Planning and Execution (Planner plus Executor). Each exposes the same interface as a single LLM agent, so primitives can be composed or swapped in place of an agent.
  number: 3 primitives
  setup: Design claim, not a measurement. An LLM "Organizer" picks and composes primitives per query. It is guided by a "Knowledge Pool" of 45 MAS structures drawn from Multi-Agent Debate, DyLAN, Self-Refine, AFlow and MAS-GPT.
  quote: "We collected a total of 45 MAS structures."
  where: p.5-6 (sec 4.2-4.3)

- claim: Headline accuracy gain over the single-agent baseline. It is the Qwen3-family range only. The two DeepSeek-distill backbones gain far less.
  number: +12.0 to +16.5 pp on Qwen3 (4B +13.9, 8B +16.5, 14B +12.0); +6.6 on R1-Distill-Qwen-32B; +6.3 on R1-Distill-Llama-70B
  setup: Average over 8 benchmarks (AIME24/25, MATH, GSM8K, HumanEval+, MBPP+, MedQA, GPQA-Diamond), 5 open backbones. The worker model and the Organizer's composition choice are tuned per query. Table 3 and Table 8 are reported once, not repeated across seeds.
  quote: "Primitives-based MAS consistently improve average accuracy by 12.0–16.5% over single-agent baselines"
  where: p.2 intro; Table 3 p.7; Table 8 p.14. The 6.3 and 6.6 gains are in the Table 3 "Avg." column.

- claim: Primitives-based MAS beats text-communicating MAS (TextMAS) on accuracy. Text MAS gains are small and vary by model.
  number: TextMAS +2.4 to +7.3 average; Primitives +16.5 on Qwen3-8B (58.8 to 75.3)
  setup: Qwen3-8B, 4 agents per TextMAS baseline.
  quote: "TextMAS yields limited average gains of 2.4%-7.3% and exhibits high variance across tasks and models"
  where: p.6 (sec 5.2)

- claim: Composing primitives beats the best single primitive, and no single primitive wins everywhere.
  number: +3.5 to +7.0 pp over the strongest individual primitive
  setup: Table 3 and Table 8. For example, on Qwen3-8B Voting averages 71.3 and the composed MAS averages 75.3.
  quote: "primitives-based MAS achieve an additional 3.5-7.0% improvement over the strongest individual primitive"
  where: p.6

- claim: Cost. Versus TextMAS, primitives-based MAS uses roughly 3-4x fewer tokens and less latency. Versus a single agent, latency is about 1.3-1.6x.
  number: tokens 3,350 vs TextMAS 14,343 (Qwen3-4B average); latency +54.5% (4B) and +52.5% (8B) vs single
  setup: Tables 13-14 (Appendix E). The token and latency numbers are not from the same runs as headline accuracy. Qwen3-14B and the DeepSeek models see Primitives tokens +/- about 0 to 14% relative to single, not -30 to -40%.
  quote: "primitives-based MAS typically reduces token usage by 30%–40% on smaller and medium-sized models"
  where: Appendix E p.16-18. Abstract claim p.1.

- claim: Primitives-based MAS beats 8 published MAS methods on Llama-3-70B-Instruct, with the largest gap on GPQA. Several published MAS methods are worse than the single agent on some benchmarks.
  number: MATH 72.4 vs Single 50.6 and MAS-GPT 68.7; HumanEval+ 82.3 vs MAS-GPT 78.9; GPQA 53.2 vs prior methods 33.6-40.2. Self-Refine on HumanEval+ is 62.7 vs Single 75.8 (-13.1). LLM-Debate on GSM8K is -0.8 and on GPQA -2.3.
  setup: Llama-3-70B-Instruct workers, GPT-5.2 Organizer. Not stated: whether the Knowledge Pool had in-domain entries for these benchmarks. The pool includes structures from these same baselines.
  quote: "The advantage of primitives-based MAS is most pronounced on GPQA, where it achieves 53.2% accuracy, surpassing prior methods (33.6-40.2%) by a large margin."
  where: Table 4, p.8 (sec 5.3)

- claim: Multi-agent token cost. Primitives uses fewer output tokens than every MAS baseline (including Organizer tokens). It is also the most cost-efficient MAS under a cost-per-accuracy metric, but not versus the single agent.
  number: Organizer adds 200-400 output tokens per query; MATH tokens: Ours 1,524 vs LLM-Debate 4,612 vs Self-Consistency 11,673 vs Single 1,375. Accuracy per $0.01 on MATH: Ours (Llama org) 258.6, Single 210.8, Ours (GPT-5.2 org) 129.3.
  setup: Llama-3-70B-Instruct; prices $1.75/1M tokens (Llama) and $14/1M tokens (GPT-5.2) output. Table 16's accuracy is identical for both Organizer settings (72.4/93.8/82.3/53.2), so it likely reuses one accuracy figure.
  quote: "the Organizer contributes only 200–400 output tokens per query (functioning as a MAS builder rather than a task solver)"
  where: Appendix F p.16-19

- claim: Motivating stress test 1. When an instruction is injected mid-context of a long document, natural-language communication follows it far less often than KV-cache communication.
  number: injection compliance at midpoint 15.6% (NL) vs 73.3% (KV); accuracy 51.6% vs 61.3% (no injection)
  setup: 351 examples from InfiniteBench En.QA, Qwen3-8B. Begin and end positions: 82.9/100 (NL) vs 88.9/100 (KV).
  quote: "injecting the instruction at the midpoint of long contexts leads to a severe drop in compliance for natural-language communication (15.6%), while KV cache communication remains substantially more robust (73.3%)."
  where: Table 1, p.4

- claim: Motivating stress test 2. Natural-language context is much more fragile to injected irrelevant sentences than KV-cache context.
  number: NL accuracy 100/91/73/47/40% at 0/1/3/10/25 noise sentences; KV 100/100/100/93/77%
  setup: 100 GSM8K problems Qwen3-8B had solved. The trace was truncated to 6,000 tokens and handed to another Qwen3-8B instance, with unrelated GSM8K reasoning sentences injected as noise, 5,000-token budget. Not realistic noise; synthetic.
  quote: "Natural Language 100% 91% 73% 47% 40%"
  where: Table 2, p.4

- claim: Ablation on the Organizer. Choosing structures randomly costs 5-12 pp; swapping GPT-5.2 for Claude-4 changes results by 0-2 pp. Without the Knowledge Pool, performance drops 5-12 pp.
  number: Random Organizer -6.6 to -12.4 pp; no Pool -4.9 to -11.9 pp; Qwen3-32B Organizer 71.3 vs 72.4 (MATH), 89.8 vs 93.8 (GSM8K), 49.1 vs 53.2 (GPQA)
  setup: Qwen3-8B and R1-Distill-Llama-70B on AIME25, HumanEval+, MedQA. Out-of-pool task (ARC-Challenge) still gets +2.3 to +2.5 pp over single without the pool, and +1.2 more with it.
  quote: "Random selection causes clear performance drops, with decreases of about 5-7% on Qwen3-8B and up to 12.4% on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-70B."
  where: Tables 5, 6, 9, 11; p.8, 14-15

- claim: Which primitive the Organizer picks depends on task type. Math favors Voting, code favors Planning, QA favors Review. Compositions use 2.5-3.4 primitives per query.
  number: Voting 52% on MATH; Planning 60% on HumanEval; Review 48% on MedQA; avg primitives 3.4 / 2.8 / 2.5
  setup: 100 examples per category.
  quote: "QA tasks rely more heavily on Review, suggesting that iterative self-correction is particularly useful when factual or domain-specific reasoning is required."
  where: Table 12, p.15-16

- claim: The latent (KV cache) channel helps independently of the primitive structure.
  number: +10.0 (Review), +10.0 (Voting), +13.4 (Planning) pp from text to KV cache
  setup: AIME25, Qwen3-8B (Text 50.0/56.7/53.3 vs KV 60.0/66.7/66.7). One benchmark and one model.
  quote: "KV-cache communication consistently improves accuracy across all three primitives (+10.0%, +10.0%, +13.4%, respectively)."
  where: Table 10, p.15

- claim: Positional re-encoding (RoPE offset) is essential when concatenating KV caches. Without it, Llama-based backbones collapse.
  number: R1-Distill-Llama-70B primitives MAS: AIME25 56.7 to 26.7; HumanEval+ 85.3 to 31.1; MedQA 81.9 to 36.6. Qwen3-8B AIME25 73.3 to 60.0.
  quote: "On the LLaMA-based model, the degradation is severe, with drops from 56.7% to 26.7% (AIME25), 85.3% to 31.1% (HumanEval+), and 81.9% to 36.6% (MedQA)."
  where: Table 7, p.8

- claim: A competing latent MAS (LatentMAS) is cheaper but unstable across backbones.
  number: R1-Distill-Llama-70B: LatentMAS -10.1 pp avg vs single; AIME24 -26.7 pp
  quote: "on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, LatentMAS reduces average accuracy by 10.1% relative to single-agent inference."
  where: p.6; Table 3 p.7

LIMITS
- KV-cache communication requires every agent to be the same model (same weights and positional encoding). The authors state this restriction directly: "we restrict our experiments to LLM agents using the same LLM to ensure valid input-output alignment." Cross-model setups are not tested. It needs access to model internals, so it does not apply to API-only models. Only open-weight models are evaluated as workers.
- Only three primitives and only reasoning-style benchmarks (math, code, QA). No tool use, no long-horizon or interactive agent tasks, and no failure analysis (nothing like Cemri et al.'s taxonomy).
- The Organizer is GPT-5.2 by default. Open-source Organizers (Qwen3-32B) lose 1-4 pp. The Knowledge Pool entries come from methods that are also baselines, which may favor the proposed method.
- No confidence intervals, seeds, or significance tests. Math sets are tiny (AIME is 30 problems, so one problem is 3.3 pp).
- Latent states are not human-readable, which they acknowledge: natural language "facilitates human interpretability and manual verification".
- The "Organizer picks the best" and "number of agents not fixed" setup means primitives-based MAS gets a variable agent count, while baselines use 4 agents. The comparison is not strictly compute-matched.

BUILDS ON
Du et al. 2023 (multi-agent debate), Madaan et al. 2023 (Self-Refine), Wang et al. 2022 (Self-Consistency), Zhang et al. 2024a (AFlow), Liu et al. 2024 (DyLAN), Ye et al. 2025 (MAS-GPT), Zhuge et al. 2024 (GPTSwarm), Hong et al. 2023 (MetaGPT), Qian et al. 2024 (ChatDev), Chen et al. 2023 (AgentVerse), Hu et al. 2024 (ADAS), Zou et al. 2025 (LatentMAS, "Latent collaboration in multi-agent systems", KV-cache latent reasoning), Fu et al. 2025 (Cache-to-Cache), Zheng et al. 2025 (ThoughtComm), Fein-Ashley et al. 2025 (Mixture of Thoughts), Su et al. 2024 (RoPE). The analogy is residual blocks (He et al. 2016) and attention (Vaswani et al. 2017).

CODE: none in the paper. Appendix A lists role prompts, for example the Critic: "You should provide targeted feedback that helps guide further improvement, but you must not revise, rewrite, or complete the solution yourself." Appendix B has the Organizer prompt, which outputs only a composition plan "in code".

FIGURES
- Fig. 1 (p.5): overview. (a) primitives-based MAS vs hand-designed MAS; (b)-(d) the three primitives; (e) Knowledge Pool; (f) KV-cache communication between two agents. It is the one picture showing how Solver/Critic, Solver/Selector and Planner/Executor exchange latent state. Not rendered here.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- Table caption faults: Table 8's caption says "Qwen3-4B and 8B" but it contains Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-14B. Table 3's caption says "three models" but covers Qwen3-8B plus the two DeepSeek distills. The extracted Table 14 repeats the DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B block under the same label twice and omits Llama-70B latency, so that latency is not available.
- Table 3 labels the "KV PoPE" ablation as "KV PoPE" in the text and "RoPE" in the table; I read it as RoPE.
- Headline numbers: the abstract's "12.0-16.5%" is for Qwen3 models only (see CLAIMS). The abstract's "3x-4x" cost reduction over TextMAS is supported by Table 13 for Qwen models (for example 14,343 vs 3,350 tokens); I did not check each model.
- Table 16 reports identical accuracy for the GPT-5.2 and Llama-3-70B Organizers.

Relevance to the target note (generative-ai/03-agentic-foundations/notes/04-multi-agent-design-patterns.md): the note's opening example is a judge that approves its own work, with a reviewer added. This paper's Review, Voting and Planning primitives correspond to reflection, voting, and plan-then-execute in the note's catalogue. Self-Refine in Table 4 gives a counter-example: it is -13.1 pp on HumanEval+ with a Llama-3-70B backbone. Natural-language handoff degradation (Tables 1-2) bears on the note's token-cost framing. I did not edit anything.
